name: Detecting Windows AD Attacks with Splunk — Event Log-Based Detection
command: index=main source="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=9 Logon_Process=seclogo | table _time, ComputerName, EventCode, user, Network_Account_Domain, Network_Account_Name, Logon_Type, Logon_Process
description: Splunk SPL queries for detecting Active Directory attacks via Windows Event Logs and SilkETW. Covers: domain recon (Sysmon EID 1 mvcount>3; SilkETW LDAP samAccountType=805306368 count>10), password spraying (EID 4625 bin 15m dc(user)), Responder/LLMNR (LLMNRDetection source; Sysmon EID 22 DNS; EID 4648 explicit logon), Kerberoasting (SilkETW SPN query; EID 4769 without prior 4648; transaction maxspan=5s closed_txn=0), AS-REProasting (EID 4768 Pre_Authentication_Type=0), Pass-the-Hash (EID 4624 Logon_Type=9 seclogo + Sysmon EID 10 LSASS transaction), Pass-the-Ticket (EID 4768/4769/4770 transaction maxspan=10h closed_txn=0), Overpass-the-Hash/Rubeus (Sysmon EID 3 dest_port=88 + EID 1 eventstats), Golden/Silver Tickets (PtT detection + EID 4672 special logon new users + user lookup baseline), Unconstrained/Constrained Delegation (PS EID 4104 TrustedForDelegation/msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo; Sysmon EID 3 port 88), DCSync (EID 4662 Replicating Directory Changes), DCShadow (EID 4742 gcspn regex).
source: CDSA Module 14: Detecting Windows Attacks with Splunk
notes:
=== MODULE CONTEXT ===
Splunk index: main | Sources: WinEventLog:Security, XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational,
  WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational, WinEventLog:SilkService-Log
SilkETW/SilkService: ETW provider wrapper that captures LDAP queries to the Windows Event Log
  → Source: WinEventLog:SilkService-Log; parse with: | spath input=Message | rename XmlEventData.* as *

=== SECTION 1 — DOMAIN RECONNAISSANCE ===

--- Native Windows Executables (Sysmon EID 1) ---
index=main source="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventID=1
  | search process_name IN (arp.exe,chcp.com,ipconfig.exe,net.exe,net1.exe,nltest.exe,ping.exe,systeminfo.exe,whoami.exe)
      OR (process_name IN (cmd.exe,powershell.exe) AND process IN (*arp*,*chcp*,*ipconfig*,*net*,*net1*,*nltest*,*ping*,*systeminfo*,*whoami*))
  | stats values(process) as process, min(_time) as _time by parent_process, parent_process_id, dest, user
  | where mvcount(process) > 3
Detects: multiple recon commands from same parent process → indicates automated recon (BloodHound, scripts)

--- BloodHound/SharpHound via SilkETW (LDAP monitoring) ---
index=main source="WinEventLog:SilkService-Log"
  | spath input=Message | rename XmlEventData.* as *
  | table _time, ComputerName, ProcessName, ProcessId, DistinguishedName, SearchFilter | sort 0 _time
  | search SearchFilter="*(samAccountType=805306368)*"
  | stats min(_time) as _time, max(_time) as maxTime, count, values(SearchFilter) as SearchFilter
      by ComputerName, ProcessName, ProcessId
  | where count > 10 | convert ctime(maxTime)
Detects: LDAP queries with samAccountType=805306368 (user accounts) — SharpHound LDAP enumeration
Note: EID 1644 is the Windows built-in LDAP performance monitor but unreliable for BloodHound detection

=== SECTION 2 — PASSWORD SPRAYING ===
index=main source="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4625
  | bin span=15m _time
  | stats values(user) as Users, dc(user) as dc_user by src, Source_Network_Address, dest, EventCode, Failure_Reason
Detects: many different users failing auth from same source IP within 15 min window
Supporting event codes: 4768+0x6 (Kerberos invalid user), 4768+0x12 (disabled user),
  4776+0xC0000064 (NTLM invalid user), 4776+0xC000006A (NTLM wrong password), 4771 (Kerberos pre-auth failed)

=== SECTION 3 — RESPONDER / LLMNR POISONING ===

--- Honeypot-based LLMNR Detection ---
# Setup: PowerShell script fires fake LLMNR queries; logs spoofed responses as custom events
# PS: New-EventLog -LogName Application -Source LLMNRDetection
# PS: Write-EventLog -LogName Application -Source LLMNRDetection -EventId 19001 -Message $msg -EntryType Warning
index=main SourceName=LLMNRDetection | table _time, ComputerName, SourceName, Message
Detects: attacker responded to LLMNR query for non-existent host

--- Sysmon DNS Query Tracking (EID 22) ---
index=main EventCode=22 | table _time, Computer, user, Image, QueryName, QueryResults
Detects: svchost.exe (LLMNR resolver) querying mistyped share names; QueryResults showing attacker IP

--- Explicit Logon to Rogue Share (EID 4648) ---
index=main EventCode IN (4648) | table _time, EventCode, source, name, user, Target_Server_Name, Message | sort 0 _time
Detects: user authenticating to attacker's rogue share (NetNTLM hash capture in progress)

=== SECTION 4 — KERBEROASTING ===

--- Benign TGS Context (for comparison) ---
index=main EventCode=4648 OR (EventCode=4769 AND service_name=iis_svc)
  | dedup RecordNumber | rex field=user "(?<username>[^@]+)"
  | table _time, ComputerName, EventCode, name, username, Account_Name, Account_Domain, src_ip,
      service_name, Ticket_Options, Ticket_Encryption_Type, Target_Server_Name, Additional_Information
Key insight: benign access generates BOTH 4648 (explicit logon) AND 4769 (TGS request)
  Kerberoasting: only 4769 without corresponding 4648

--- SPN Query Detection via SilkETW ---
index=main source="WinEventLog:SilkService-Log"
  | spath input=Message | rename XmlEventData.* as *
  | table _time, ComputerName, ProcessName, DistinguishedName, SearchFilter
  | search SearchFilter="*(&(samAccountType=805306368)(servicePrincipalName=*)*"
Detects: LDAP queries for accounts with SPNs — Kerberoasting target enumeration phase

--- TGS Request Without Prior Logon (Stats Method) ---
index=main EventCode=4648 OR (EventCode=4769 AND service_name=iis_svc)
  | dedup RecordNumber | rex field=user "(?<username>[^@]+)" | bin span=2m _time | search username!=*$
  | stats values(EventCode) as Events, values(service_name) as service_name,
      values(Additional_Information) as Additional_Information, values(Target_Server_Name) as Target_Server_Name
      by _time, username
  | where !match(Events,"4648")
Detects: EID 4769 present but EID 4648 absent within 2-min window = Kerberoasting

--- TGS Without Prior Logon (Transaction Method) ---
index=main EventCode=4648 OR (EventCode=4769 AND service_name=iis_svc)
  | dedup RecordNumber | rex field=user "(?<username>[^@]+)" | search username!=*$
  | transaction username keepevicted=true maxspan=5s endswith=(EventCode=4648) startswith=(EventCode=4769)
  | where closed_txn=0 AND EventCode = 4769
  | table _time, EventCode, service_name, username
Detects: 4769 that started but never got a 4648 within 5 seconds

=== SECTION 4 (cont.) — AS-REProasting ===

--- Pre-Auth Disabled Account Discovery via SilkETW ---
index=main source="WinEventLog:SilkService-Log"
  | spath input=Message | rename XmlEventData.* as *
  | table _time, ComputerName, ProcessName, DistinguishedName, SearchFilter
  | search SearchFilter="*(samAccountType=805306368)(userAccountControl:1.2.840.113556.1.4.803:=4194304)*"
Detects: LDAP query for users with DONT_REQ_PREAUTH bit set (0x400000 = 4194304)

--- AS-REP Roasting TGT Request Detection (EID 4768) ---
index=main source="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4768 Pre_Authentication_Type=0
  | rex field=src_ip "(\:\:ffff\:)?(?<src_ip>[0-9\.]+)"
  | table _time, src_ip, user, Pre_Authentication_Type, Ticket_Options, Ticket_Encryption_Type
Detects: TGT request with Pre_Authentication_Type=0 (no pre-auth required) = AS-REPRoasting target
Note: Ticket_Encryption_Type=0x17 (RC4-HMAC) = weaker, crackable hash

=== SECTION 5 — PASS-THE-HASH ===

--- Basic PtH Detection (EID 4624 LogonType=9 with seclogo) ---
index=main source="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=9 Logon_Process=seclogo
  | table _time, ComputerName, EventCode, user, Network_Account_Domain, Network_Account_Name, Logon_Type, Logon_Process
Detects: LogonType=9 (NewCredentials) + Logon_Process=seclogo = Mimikatz PtH
False positives: legitimate runas /netonly usage

--- Enhanced PtH: Correlate LSASS Access + NewCredentials Logon ---
index=main
  (source="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=10
    TargetImage="C:\\Windows\\system32\\lsass.exe"
    SourceImage!="C:\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\platform\\*\\MsMpEng.exe")
  OR (source="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=9 Logon_Process=seclogo)
  | sort _time, RecordNumber
  | transaction host maxspan=1m endswith=(EventCode=4624) startswith=(EventCode=10)
  | stats count by _time, Computer, SourceImage, SourceProcessId,
      Network_Account_Domain, Network_Account_Name, Logon_Type, Logon_Process
  | fields - count
Detects: Mimikatz LSASS memory read (EID 10) followed by NewCredentials logon within 1 min = PtH confirmed

=== SECTION 6 — PASS-THE-TICKET ===
index=main source="WinEventLog:Security" user!=*$ EventCode IN (4768,4769,4770)
  | rex field=user "(?<username>[^@]+)"
  | rex field=src_ip "(\:\:ffff\:)?(?<src_ip_4>[0-9\.]+)"
  | transaction username, src_ip_4 maxspan=10h keepevicted=true startswith=(EventCode=4768)
  | where closed_txn=0
  | search NOT user="*$@*"
  | table _time, ComputerName, username, src_ip_4, service_name, category
Logic: PtT = host requests TGS (4769/4770) WITHOUT a prior TGT request (4768) from same host
  → transaction starts with 4768; if no 4768 found but 4769/4770 present = open transaction (closed_txn=0)
  → keepevicted=true includes incomplete transactions
Event IDs: 4768=TGT Request, 4769=TGS Request, 4770=TGS Renewal

=== SECTION 7 — OVERPASS-THE-HASH (Targeting Rubeus) ===
index=main source="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational"
  (EventCode=3 dest_port=88 Image!=*lsass.exe) OR EventCode=1
  | eventstats values(process) as process by process_id
  | where EventCode=3
  | stats count by _time, Computer, dest_ip, dest_port, Image, process
  | fields - count
Detects: Non-lsass.exe process making TCP/UDP connection to port 88 (Kerberos) = Rubeus AS-REQ
  eventstats enriches EID 3 (network event) with full command line from EID 1 (process create)
Note: Mimikatz OPtH leaves same PtH artifacts; Rubeus OPtH generates EID 4768 (unlike PtT)

=== SECTION 8 — GOLDEN TICKETS / SILVER TICKETS ===

--- Golden Ticket: Same PtT Detection ---
# Uses same EID 4768/4769/4770 transaction query as Section 6
# Golden Ticket: forged TGT imported — no prior 4768 from attacker system on DC
# Offline forgery means virtually no Mimikatz EID traces

--- Silver Ticket: New User Baseline Approach ---
# Step 1: Create users.csv from account creation events
index=main latest=<timestamp> EventCode=4720
  | stats min(_time) as _time, values(EventCode) as EventCode by user
  | outputlookup users.csv

# Step 2: Find logins for users NOT in the baseline (non-existent users = Silver Ticket)
index=main latest=<timestamp> EventCode=4624
  | stats min(_time) as firstTime, values(ComputerName) as ComputerName, values(EventCode) as EventCode by user
  | eval last24h = <epoch_24h_ago>
  | where firstTime > last24h
  | convert ctime(firstTime)
  | lookup users.csv user as user OUTPUT EventCode as Events
  | where isnull(Events)
Detects: users logged in within last 24h who don't appear in EID 4720 (account creation) events

--- Silver Ticket: Special Privileges Detection (EID 4672) ---
index=main latest=<timestamp> EventCode=4672
  | stats min(_time) as firstTime, values(ComputerName) as ComputerName by Account_Name
  | eval last24h = <epoch_24h_ago>
  | where firstTime > last24h
  | table firstTime, ComputerName, Account_Name | convert ctime(firstTime)
Detects: new accounts getting special logon privileges (SeDebugPrivilege etc.) in last 24h

=== SECTION 9 — UNCONSTRAINED/CONSTRAINED DELEGATION ===

--- Unconstrained Delegation Discovery via PowerShell Logging (EID 4104) ---
index=main source="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational" EventCode=4104
  Message="*TrustedForDelegation*" OR Message="*userAccountControl:1.2.840.113556.1.4.803:=524288*"
  | table _time, ComputerName, EventCode, Message
Detects: PowerShell querying for TrustedForDelegation attribute (0x80000 = 524288 = TRUSTED_FOR_DELEGATION bit)

--- Constrained Delegation Discovery (EID 4104) ---
index=main source="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational" EventCode=4104
  Message="*msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo*" | table _time, ComputerName, EventCode, Message

--- Constrained Delegation Attack: Rubeus Port 88 (Sysmon EID 3) ---
index=main source="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational"
  | eventstats values(process) as process by process_id
  | where EventCode=3 AND dest_port=88
  | table _time, Computer, dest_ip, dest_port, Image, process
Detects: Rubeus connecting to DC port 88 for S4U2self/S4U2proxy TGS requests
Note: S4U2self = impersonate any user; S4U2proxy = escalate to target SPN

=== SECTION 10 — DCSYNC / DCSHADOW ===

--- DCSync Detection (EID 4662) ---
index=main EventCode=4662 Message="*Replicating Directory Changes*"
  | rex field=Message "(?P<property>Replicating Directory Changes.*)"
  | table _time, user, object_file_name, Object_Server, property
Detects: DS-Replication-Get-Changes operations (GUID: {1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2})
Prerequisite: Enable 'Audit Directory Service Access' in Advanced Audit Policy
Note: EID 4662 only contains GUIDs; use rex to extract readable property names

--- DCShadow Detection (EID 4742) ---
index=main EventCode=4742
  | rex field=Message "(?P<gcspn>XX\/[a-zA-Z0-9\.\-\/]+)"
  | table _time, ComputerName, Security_ID, Account_Name, user, gcspn
  | search gcspn=*
Detects: Computer account SPN changes containing global catalog (GC) SPN
  DCShadow must add: nTDSDSA object + global catalog SPN to computer object
  Real DC has GC SPN "GC/..." but XX represents the 2-char prefix used in the module query
Note: Change XX to actual GC prefix to match your environment

=== SECTION 11 — CUSTOM SPLUNK APPLICATIONS ===
Creating a custom Splunk app to house detection dashboards:
1. Apps → Manage Apps → Create app
   Name: <App name> | Folder: <app_name> | Template: barebones
2. App directory: $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/<app_name>/
   /bin (scripts), /default (config/views/nav), /local (user overrides), /metadata (permissions)
3. Navigation file: $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/<app>/default/data/ui/nav/default.xml
4. Create dashboards: Dashboards → Create New → Classic Dashboards
   Use time input token ($time$), add Statistical Table panel with SPL search string
5. Dashboard XML stored at: <AppPath>/local/data/ui/views/<dashboard_name>.xml
6. Group dashboards with <collection> tag in default.xml nav
7. Install pre-built app: Apps → Manage Apps → Install app from file (check "Upgrade app")

=== KEY EVENT ID REFERENCE ===
EID 1 (Sysmon): Process Create
EID 3 (Sysmon): Network Connection (dest_port=88 = Kerberos)
EID 10 (Sysmon): Process Access (TargetImage=lsass.exe = credential dumping)
EID 22 (Sysmon): DNS Query (QueryName=mistyped share = LLMNR poisoning)
EID 4104 (PS): Script Block Logging (PowerShell LDAP queries)
EID 4624 (Security): Logon Success (Logon_Type=9 = NewCredentials = PtH)
EID 4625 (Security): Logon Failure (dc(user)>6 from same IP = password spraying)
EID 4648 (Security): Explicit Credential Logon (missing when Kerberoasting)
EID 4662 (Security): Object Access on AD object (DCSync replication)
EID 4668 (Security): TGT Renewal
EID 4720 (Security): User Account Created (baseline for Silver Ticket detection)
EID 4742 (Security): Computer Account Changed (DCShadow SPN modification)
EID 4768 (Security): Kerberos TGT Request (missing in PtT; Pre_Auth_Type=0 in AS-REP)
EID 4769 (Security): Kerberos TGS Request (missing 4648 pair = Kerberoasting)
EID 4770 (Security): Kerberos TGS Renewal
EID 4672 (Security): Special Privileges Assigned to New Logon

=== SPLUNK TRANSACTION COMMAND PATTERNS ===
# Find open/incomplete transactions (startswith found but endswith not):
| transaction <groupby_field> keepevicted=true maxspan=<time> startswith=(<filter>) [endswith=(<filter>)]
| where closed_txn=0
→ closed_txn=0 = transaction opened but never closed = attack pattern

# PtT specific: TGS without prior TGT
| transaction username, src_ip_4 maxspan=10h keepevicted=true startswith=(EventCode=4768)
| where closed_txn=0  → 4769/4770 without prior 4768 = ticket imported (PtT)

# Kerberoasting specific: TGS without explicit credential logon
| transaction username keepevicted=true maxspan=5s startswith=(EventCode=4769) endswith=(EventCode=4648)
| where closed_txn=0 AND EventCode=4769

examples.label: Detect domain recon — multiple native tools from same parent process
examples.command: index=main source="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventID=1 | search process_name IN (arp.exe,net.exe,nltest.exe,whoami.exe,systeminfo.exe) | stats values(process) as process, min(_time) as _time by parent_process, parent_process_id, dest, user | where mvcount(process) > 3

examples.label: Detect BloodHound LDAP enumeration via SilkETW
examples.command: index=main source="WinEventLog:SilkService-Log" | spath input=Message | rename XmlEventData.* as * | search SearchFilter="*(samAccountType=805306368)*" | stats min(_time) as _time, count, values(SearchFilter) as SearchFilter by ComputerName, ProcessName, ProcessId | where count > 10

examples.label: Detect password spraying — many users failing from same IP
examples.command: index=main source="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4625 | bin span=15m _time | stats values(user) as Users, dc(user) as dc_user by src, Source_Network_Address, dest, EventCode, Failure_Reason

examples.label: Detect AS-REProasting — TGT requests without pre-authentication
examples.command: index=main source="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4768 Pre_Authentication_Type=0 | rex field=src_ip "(\:\:ffff\:)?(?<src_ip>[0-9\.]+)" | table _time, src_ip, user, Pre_Authentication_Type, Ticket_Options, Ticket_Encryption_Type

examples.label: Detect Pass-the-Hash — NewCredentials logon via seclogo process
examples.command: index=main source="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=9 Logon_Process=seclogo | table _time, ComputerName, EventCode, user, Network_Account_Domain, Network_Account_Name, Logon_Type, Logon_Process

examples.label: Detect Pass-the-Hash (enhanced) — LSASS access correlated with NewCredentials logon
examples.command: index=main (source="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=10 TargetImage="C:\\Windows\\system32\\lsass.exe" SourceImage!="C:\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\platform\\*\\MsMpEng.exe") OR (source="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=9 Logon_Process=seclogo) | sort _time, RecordNumber | transaction host maxspan=1m endswith=(EventCode=4624) startswith=(EventCode=10) | stats count by _time, Computer, SourceImage, SourceProcessId, Network_Account_Domain, Network_Account_Name, Logon_Type, Logon_Process | fields - count

examples.label: Detect Pass-the-Ticket — TGS/renewal without prior TGT from same host
examples.command: index=main source="WinEventLog:Security" user!=*$ EventCode IN (4768,4769,4770) | rex field=user "(?<username>[^@]+)" | rex field=src_ip "(\:\:ffff\:)?(?<src_ip_4>[0-9\.]+)" | transaction username, src_ip_4 maxspan=10h keepevicted=true startswith=(EventCode=4768) | where closed_txn=0 | search NOT user="*$@*" | table _time, ComputerName, username, src_ip_4, service_name, category

examples.label: Detect Overpass-the-Hash (Rubeus) — non-lsass process connecting to Kerberos port 88
examples.command: index=main source="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" (EventCode=3 dest_port=88 Image!=*lsass.exe) OR EventCode=1 | eventstats values(process) as process by process_id | where EventCode=3 | stats count by _time, Computer, dest_ip, dest_port, Image, process | fields - count

examples.label: Detect Kerberoasting — TGS request without preceding explicit credential logon (transaction)
examples.command: index=main EventCode=4648 OR (EventCode=4769 AND service_name=iis_svc) | dedup RecordNumber | rex field=user "(?<username>[^@]+)" | search username!=*$ | transaction username keepevicted=true maxspan=5s endswith=(EventCode=4648) startswith=(EventCode=4769) | where closed_txn=0 AND EventCode = 4769 | table _time, EventCode, service_name, username

examples.label: Detect DCSync — directory replication changes by non-DC account
examples.command: index=main EventCode=4662 Message="*Replicating Directory Changes*" | rex field=Message "(?P<property>Replicating Directory Changes.*)" | table _time, user, object_file_name, Object_Server, property

examples.label: Detect DCShadow — rogue DC registration via computer account SPN change
examples.command: index=main EventCode=4742 | rex field=Message "(?P<gcspn>GC\/[a-zA-Z0-9\.\-\/]+)" | table _time, ComputerName, Security_ID, Account_Name, user, gcspn | search gcspn=*

examples.label: Detect unconstrained delegation discovery via PowerShell script block logging
examples.command: index=main source="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational" EventCode=4104 Message="*TrustedForDelegation*" OR Message="*userAccountControl:1.2.840.113556.1.4.803:=524288*" | table _time, ComputerName, EventCode, Message
